title: Fourier coefficients of randomization
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $f$ be real-valued on its outcome space, fix an outcome $x$, and let $S\subseteq[n]$. The Walsh--Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the function $r\mapsto R_rf(x)$ is the $S$-component of $f$ evaluated at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with strictly positive atom masses
$f$ is a real-valued function on the outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $x\in\Omega$, and $S\subseteq[n]$. The Walsh coefficient at $S$ of $r\mapsto R_rf(x)=\sum_T\chi_T(r)f_T(x)$ is $f_S(x)$.
